text_summary.body: Forces from him profane the sanctuary, take away the continual burnt offering and set up the abomination that makes desolate. (Daniel names no king; 1 Maccabees narrates the event.)

setting.body: After his return from Egypt Antiochus IV plundered the Temple (1 Macc 1:20–24, year 143); later a royal decree banned Jewish practice, and on 15 Chislev 145 an "abomination of desolation" was built on the altar, with pagan sacrifice from 25 Chislev (1 Macc 1:54, 59). Josephus dates it to 145 SE in the 153rd Olympiad.

constraints.textual_assertion: After his return from Egypt … the king sent letters … that they should profane the sanctuary (1 Macc 1:20–54)
assumptions: 1 Maccabees places the plunder of the Temple after the first Egyptian campaign (143 SE) and the desecration two years later; Jerome says the profanation came two years after the plunder.

constraints.textual_assertion: at the time and on the day the Gentiles had profaned it, on that day it was dedicated (1 Macc 4:54)
assumptions: From 15 Chislev 145 to 25 Chislev 148: three years and ten days (Driver); 36–38 months allows for intercalary months.
